sentences.text: Edentosuchus is a member of the protosuchian crocodyliform group.
This creature possessed markedly heterodont teeth, meaning its teeth varied significantly in shape.
The teeth at the tip of the upper jaw were conical, while the first two behind the tip had three cusps.
The skull was only a few centimetres long, featuring a short, relatively narrow snout and a wide posterior section.
The fifth and last upper jaw tooth was bulbous, larger than the others, and featured small cusps.
The type species is Edentosuchus tienshanensis.
A joint expedition between the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County and the National Geological Museum of China recovered another partial skull in 2000.
New fossil material of Edentosuchus tienshanensis from the Lower Cretaceous Lianmuqin Formation was described by Tan et al. in 2026.
While originally placed in its own family, later research determined Edentosuchus belongs to the family Protosuchidae.
Edentosuchus is classified within the parent group Protosuchidae.
Fossils of Edentosuchus come from the Early Cretaceous Tugulu Group in the Junggar Basin of Xinjiang, China.
Edentosuchus lived between 199.5 and 184.2 million years ago during the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages.
Contemporary fauna included turtles, dsungaripterid pterosaurs, and various dinosaurs such as theropods, sauropods, stegosaurs, psittacosaurids, and ornithopods.
